newsitem.title: USA: Dole deflects age issue in debate with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Dole deflects age issue in debate with Clinton.

text.p: Republican candidate Bob Dole tried on Wednesday to deflect concern that he may be too old to be elected U.S. president with humour, saying age and experience were the keys to wisdom.

Asked by a woman student during a televised debate with President Bill Clinton how he would relate to concerns of young people, the 73-year-old Dole drew a laugh when he said: "I think you know wisdom comes from age, experience and intelligence ... I have some age, some wisdom, some experience and some intelligence -- that adds up to wisdom."

In response, Clinton, 50, appeared at first to compliment Dole, saying: "I don't think Senator Dole is too old to be president." But he followed up with sharp riposte: "It's the age of his ideas that I question."
Polls have shown that a significant number of voters question Dole's fitness for the rigorous office of president.

To try to head off such concerns, Dole, who still suffers from the affects of wounds suffered during World War Two, has made public his full medical records and frequently says he is at least as fit as his younger opponent.
The clash came during the final televised debate between Dole and Clinton 20 days before the election.
